subject: Request: temporary latency SLO variance during large model re-indexing
messages:
From: Gretchen Kline <gretchen@heliosbio.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary latency SLO variance during large model re-indexing

Hi Tessa / Marissa,

We're planning a 3-week re-index and model retraining window starting next Monday that will push significant batch traffic through the Redwood endpoints used for our production inference pipeline. Early simulations indicate our 95th percentile latency will spike for short periods (90-120 minutes/day) during the first week while we warm caches and migrate KV data.

Can we request a temporary variance to the latency SLO (increase 95p target from 250ms to 900ms during the maintenance window) for up to 4 weeks and a capped remediation/credit approach during that time? Procurement asked me to surface a proposed remedy so we can keep the integration moving without pausing experiments.

What Helios is willing to accept: a formal variance window, explicit start/end dates, and a capped service credit (no more than 5% MRR for the month in question). We don't want to trigger contract termination or broader remedies.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call to walk through the plan.

Gretchen Kline
Director, Platform Engineering
Helios Biotech
procurement@heliosbio.com
Attachment: helios-reindex-plan.pdf (attached)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency SLO variance during large model re-indexing

Thanks Gretchen — cc'ing internal owners to capture next steps. Summary / ask: Helios requests a 4-week variance starting 2027-03-08 for increased 95p latency during scheduled re-indexing and a capped credit (<=5% MRR) in any affected month. They need formal sign-off to proceed.

My read: this is a predictable, scheduled operational event tied to customer activity; we can offer a limited, documented variance + a pragmatic credit cap if legal & finance accept wording. Proposed remedy (attached) is a short amendment: 4-week variance window, explicit exclusion for scheduled maintenance spikes during the specified window, credits capped at 5% MRR, mandatory post-window evaluation and mitigation plan.

Ask: Legal to confirm redline risks / required indemnities. Finance to confirm cap tolerance. Infra to verify monitoring and rollback controls. If we agree, this needs executive signoff for an exception to standard SLA language.

Attachments: proposed_remedy_helios_20270303.pdf

Next steps suggested:
- Jonas: quick legal review and redline by 2027-03-04 EOD
- Rishi & Vivek: confirm monitoring/auto-fallback + one-sentence mitigation plan by 2027-03-04 noon
- Lauren: confirm commercial approval for 5% cap by 2027-03-04 EOD
- If all green, escalate to Aditya for exec signoff 2027-03-05

Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency SLO variance during large model re-indexing

Tessa — quick legal read below and attached redlines. High-level: we can accept a temporary variance but with the following guardrails: 

1) Credit cap must be contractual and limited to an explicit percentage of monthly recurring revenue (your 5% is reasonable).
2) Add a clause that this variance applies only to the agreed window and does not change baseline SLA obligations outside that window.
3) Require Helios to acknowledge maintenance schedule in writing and indemnify Redwood for any third-party impacts caused by Helios-initiated batch activity (simple narrow language).
4) Require monitoring & post-mortem within 7 business days of the window close, with remediation commitments.

I attached a tracked redline of the amendment (legal_redlines_jonas_20270304.docx). I'm not comfortable with open-ended language or anything that dilutes core uptime covenants beyond the stated window.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: legal_redlines_jonas_20270304.docx

Team — finance view: we can accept a 5% MRR cap for a one-off scheduled maintenance window tied to customer activity. Conditions:

- Cap needs to be written into the amendment and reference the covered month clearly.
- Credits cannot stack with other negotiated concessions.
- We want an explicit monitoring dashboard export (CSV) proof-of-impact for any credit claim.

If legal agrees to Jonas' redlines and infra commits to the monitoring + rollback plan, finance signs off. From a commercial tolerance perspective, this is preferable to pausing the Helios rollout.

Thanks all for the clear summary. I reviewed the proposed amendment, Jonas' redlines, and Lauren's commercial conditions. Exec decision: APPROVED with conditions.

Conditions for approval:
- Variance window approved: 2027-03-08 to 2027-04-05 (4 weeks).
- Credit cap: 5% of MRR for the impacted month.
- Written maintenance schedule from Helios required 48 hours prior to the start of the window.
- Legal redlines accepted; require Helios acknowledgment & indemnity language.
- Infra must publish the monitoring dashboard export and the post-window remediation report within 7 business days of close.

Tessa / Marissa: please prepare the amendment incorporating the redlines and send for signature via DocuSign (use attached HubSpot deal HB-9342). Once signed, confirm update to the customer's onboarding timeline.
